description: Not a corpus entry: a fixture for the writer refusal, which no entry of the corpus can state. Its header is keyed on the three bytes a detail's packed amount occupies, so the pair rests on the order; the detail carries the lenient sign nibble A, which is positive, so the reader routes it to the detail and reports the values below -- and a writer handed that record back emits the canonical nibble C, which is the header's literal, at a state where the header's test is ordered first. The reading direction is what this file says, and it is right; the writing direction refuses, which is what the test that loads this fixture asserts.
source: docs/ir/SPEC.md, "A writer walks the same automaton" -- the check a writer owes at a state carrying the pair "A batch boundary is told by the order" admits -- with "When two match, and when none does", which declines a byte domain for a packed item; the lenient sign nibble is cobol-go codec/SPEC.md, Appendix A, and testdata/conformance/packed-ascii carries it
